recall_prompt: Say how you would count the chains from seven different beads — why the circular count is halved, and the number.
insider_note: Same two lines as the 6-bead chain — only the number changes: (7 − 1)!/2 = 720/2 = 360. The halving still carries the mark; 720 alone counts a ring that cannot be turned over.

steps.label: A chain is a circular arrangement that can be turned over
steps.margin_note: First mark. Beads on a chain form a circle, so (n − 1)! arrangements; a chain can be turned over, so halve it: (n − 1)!/2.

recall.must_convey: That beads on a chain are a circular arrangement, (n minus 1) factorial, halved because the chain can be turned over.
accept: circular arrangement is n minus one factorial and a chain can be flipped so divide by two
n minus one factorial by two because clockwise and anticlockwise are the same chain
a chain is a circle that can be turned over so half of n minus one factorial
circle ki n minus one factorial, chain ni flip cheyochu kabatti by two
the formula for chains is n minus one factorial over two

steps.why: Rotations of a circle give the same arrangement, so (n − 1)!; turning the chain over makes each arrangement and its mirror image one chain, so a further half.
common_mistakes: Using n! as for a row.

steps.label: Evaluate for n = 7

accept: six factorial by two is three hundred sixty
seven twenty by two is three sixty
six factorial by two three hundred sixty
the answer is three hundred and sixty chains

steps.why: With n = 7, (n − 1)! = 720 and half of it is 360.
